_schema: The GPS module — plans/2026-09-12-control-room-design.md §2.3, slice C1. Two tiers, as in every other catalog file: `specs` is physics-bearing and `catalog` is browsing metadata only. Colour, price and vendor links are banned by name, from either block. WHAT THE PHYSICS READS IS THE MASS, THE THREE BOX DIMENSIONS AND `mast_height_mm`. Everything else here is a string a builder browses on. `mast_height_mm` IS THE REASON THIS CATEGORY EXISTS rather than a few grams added to the harness remainder: a masted GPS puts its mass ABOVE THE TOP PLATE ON A STALK, which makes it the highest mass on the aircraft and the single thing fitted that moves the centre of mass VERTICALLY more than anything else. A flat module carries 0 and sits on the plate; a masted one carries the stalk's real height. MassProperties already has the machinery — the module only has to sit where it really sits — so getting this field wrong is not a rounding error, it is mass in the wrong place. It ships as an EDITABLE DEFAULT, because a mast's height is a builder's choice and not a product specification. `constellations`, `compass` and `protocol` are in `catalog` and reach NOTHING: there is no navigation, no position hold, no return-to-home and no magnetometer model in Lothal, and a GPS here is mass, height, and a port on the flight controller. Claiming otherwise would be inventing a spec to unlock a feature. Entries are ordered by mass. THE MASSES AND MAST HEIGHTS HERE ARE CLASS-TYPICAL RATHER THAN VENDOR-SOURCED, and each entry's `source` says so in the guess voice — design §0 relaxed the bar on values and not on honesty.

parts.name: Micro GPS, flat
parts.source: class-typical 16 x 16 mm flat micro module of the kind taped to a toothpick or 3" top plate, not a specific product. Mass is ROUGH — sub-5 g modules rarely publish one, and the figure moves with how much of the pigtail you count. mast_height_mm is 0 because this class has no stalk at all.

parts.name: Compact GPS + compass, flat
parts.source: class-typical 20 x 20 mm flat module with a magnetometer on the board, the commonest thing fitted to a 5" freestyle build that wants a rescue mode. Mass is ROUGH and class-typical, not a specific product.

parts.name: Standard GPS + compass, flat
parts.source: class-typical 25 x 25 mm flat module — the larger patch antenna is where the extra grams are, and it is fitted flat on a 7" top plate where there is room for it. Mass is ROUGH and class-typical, not a specific product.

parts.name: Masted GPS + compass, short mast
parts.source: class-typical masted module: a 20-odd mm board on a short folding stalk, fitted to get the magnetometer away from the ESC's current path. Mass includes the mast and its base. THE 45 mm MAST HEIGHT IS A ROUGH DEFAULT, not a specification — folding stalks are cut to length by the builder, and design §2.3 says the editable field beside it is the real answer.

parts.name: Long-range GPS + compass, tall mast
parts.source: class-typical long-range module on a tall stalk, the heaviest thing in this file and deliberately so: 14 g at 70 mm above the top plate is the case design §2.3 exists to make visible. Mass and mast height are both ROUGH class-typical figures, not a specific product.

parts.name: Dronetag Beacon (broadcast Remote ID)
parts.source: Dronetag Beacon product page, https://dronetag.com/products/beacon/ (read 2026-11-13). PUBLISHED: 16 g, 37 x 26 x 16 mm, Li-Po 3.7 V 200 mAh internal battery, current 15 mA avg / 100 mA peak; resellers (getfpv, Drone Nerds) agree on 16 g, one Adorama Gen 2 listing says 17 g. A broadcast Remote ID add-on, NOT a navigation GNSS: do not fit it in the gps slot. Power: it runs on its own cell, so it draws nothing from the flight pack; the survey-kit builds nevertheless charge 0.37 W (= 100 mA peak x 3.7 V, computed from the published figures, an upper bound) to the pack so the option is never free. ROUGH: the strap mount and the 0.37 W charged to the flight pack are our own assumptions, not maker figures; only the mass, box, cell and current are published.

parts.name: RTK GNSS module, mast-mounted
parts.source: class-typical multi-band RTK GNSS receiver with patch antenna of the kind fitted to survey multirotors, not a specific product. Mass, box and 40 mm mast are ESTIMATED / unverified class figures; no manufacturer sheet was consulted.

parts.name: Here3+ RTK GNSS (CAN)
parts.source: CubePilot Here3 manual, https://docs.cubepilot.org/user-guides/here-3/here-3-manual . PUBLISHED: Here3+ 51.8 g (Here3 is 48.8 g), 68 x 68 x 16 mm, RTK accuracy 0.025 m. Mast height 0 mm is a ROUGH class-typical ESTIMATE (sits flat on the top plate; a mast would add mass and height). RTK needs a base station or network, not modelled.
